textbookBox.concept: Carbon has four valence electrons, so it cannot easily lose or gain four. Instead it shares electrons in covalent bonds.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Carbon has four valence electrons, so it cannot easily lose or gain four. Instead it shares electrons in covalent bonds.
beats.speakEn: Carbon has four valence electrons, so it cannot easily lose or gain four. Instead it shares electrons in covalent bonds.

beats.en: In methane CH4, carbon shares one electron with each of four hydrogens. Covalent compounds usually have low melting and boiling points and are poor conductors.
beats.speakEn: In methane CH4, carbon shares one electron with each of four hydrogens. Covalent compounds usually have low melting and boiling points and are poor conductors.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 10 science · Carbon and its Compounds · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Saturated compounds have only single bonds, like alkanes CnH2n+2. Unsaturated compounds have double (alkenes CnH2n) or triple (alkynes CnH2n-2) bonds.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Carbon and its Compounds: Saturated compounds have only single bonds, like alkanes CnH2n+2. Unsaturated compounds have double (alkenes CnH2n) or triple (alkynes CnH2n-2) bonds.
